HIV attacks the body's immune system, specifically the CD4 cells (T-cells), which help the body fight off infections and diseases. Over time, HIV can weaken the immune system to the point where the body can no longer fight off infections and diseases, leading to AIDS.

Treatment for AIDS typically involves antiretroviral therapy (ART). ART is a combination of medications that work together to reduce the amount of HIV in the body.
